name: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Muḥammad al-Ḍabbī
summary: Kufan transmitter of the old poetry, trusted even by the Basran Abū Zayd, who gathered for the caliph al-Mahdī the anthology of early odes called al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls al-Mufaḍḍal trustworthy and one of the great men of Kufa: the Basran Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī took from him for his reliability. For the caliph al-Mahdī he collected the chosen odes known after him as al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt, whose number varies from copy to copy; the soundest recension, Ibn al-Anbārī says, is the one Ibn al-Aʿrābī transmitted.
Al-Zubaydī counts him in the second generation of the lexicographers of Kufa.
uncertain: Ibn al-Anbārī gives no year of death; TDV gives about 168/784, others 170/786 or 178/794.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 67–69
